subtitle: Lesson 26 · Storage & Data Loading at Scale

steps.label: Object (S3)
steps.sub: cheap, durable source of truth; real per-request latency

steps.label: Block (EBS)
steps.sub: fast, but attached to one instance — not shared

steps.label: Parallel FS (FSx Lustre)
steps.sub: POSIX filesystem many nodes mount at once

steps.label: FSx for Lustre
steps.sub: up to hundreds of GB/s aggregate, 700 Gbps/client with EFA

eyebrow: A cache in front of the source of truth
code:
# S3 is durable storage for every shard ever produced
s3://solara-checkpoints-data/shards/

# FSx for Lustre: linked via a data repository
# association (DRA), lazily loads on first read
fsx_mount = "/mnt/solara-fsx/shards/"
# first read -> pulled from S3, cached on FSx SSD
# every read after -> served from FSx, low latency
caption: An S3 data repository association lazily loads objects into FSx for Lustre the first time a job reads them.

subtitle: When the storage layer isn't the problem, but the loader still is.
